frequency_question: How often does a partisan majority in a legislative chamber successfully pass its core restrictive electoral integrity bills through its own floor within a single session?
membership_rule: Bills explicitly requiring documentary proof of citizenship or similar restrictive identity verification for federal voter registration passed by a chamber controlled by the sponsoring party, excluding broader omnibus bills that lacked standalone votes.

cases.name: For the People Act / Freedom to Vote Act variants (Democratic majority priority)
SAVE Act House Passage (Republican majority priority)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named; represents the full population of standalone federal voting integrity/restrictive bills brought to chamber floor votes by partisan majorities in recent sessions.
known_gaps: Excludes committee-only stalls where leadership chose not to spend floor time.
skeleton: Legislative chambers passing chamber-priority partisan bills when the sponsoring party holds unified control or strong caucus alignment on the specific issue
multiplier: 2 hits out of 2 major attempts at narrow partisan voting integrity bills brought to a floor vote by the respective majority leadership.
validity_reason: Remains valid through the current 119th Congress until a new congressional alignment takes office.
